changes.before: Buddy just barked and tried to lick the safety netting.
changes.after: Buddy just barked and tried to lick the safety netting. It tasted of rope. He tried a second square before accepting the result.

changes.before: Buddy leaped in and started pawing at the brake lever.
changes.after: Buddy leaped in and started pawing at the brake lever. Sagar moved his hand over it. Buddy placed his paw on top, volunteering for management.

changes.after: Buddy tried to chase a shooting star (it was a flashlight). The bright spot climbed a tree. Buddy stopped at the trunk and looked back, offended by this change in the rules.

changes.before: Buddy joined in, barking “You tell ‘em, Neet! This is a democracy!”
changes.after:
Buddy joined in, barking “You tell ‘em, Neet! This is a democracy!”

One turkey stopped to peck the ground. Neet started again, louder. The turkey found another seed.

changes.before: Neet found the old oak he’d once claimed as his “Royal Throne.” Buddy rolled in the dirt, happy to be home, even just for a moment.
changes.after: Neet found the old oak he’d once claimed as his “Royal Throne.” Buddy rolled in the dirt, happy to be home, even just for a moment. When Heather mentioned the duck pond again, he stopped rolling long enough to check which way it was.

changes.before: Buddy, sensing excitement, barked at the luggage, the door, his own tail, and then at the Keurig for good measure.
changes.after: Buddy, sensing excitement, barked at the luggage, the door, his own tail, and then at the Keurig for good measure. The Keurig gurgled back. Buddy planted himself in front of it. Apparently there was time for one more argument.

changes.before: Buddy farted loudly, and the journey was underway.
changes.after: Buddy farted loudly, and the journey was underway. Heather lowered her window. Neet lowered his opinion of the middle seat.

changes.before: Buddy barked encouragement. “Come on, Neet! Pretend there’s pizza on the other side!”
changes.after:
Buddy barked encouragement. “Come on, Neet! Pretend there’s pizza on the other side!”

Neet lifted one paw. “Is there?”

Buddy looked toward the far platform. He had meant to help. Now he wanted to know too.

changes.before: Buddy tried to stash a crust for later but Sagar gently reclaimed it with a smile.
changes.after: Buddy tried to stash a crust for later but Sagar gently reclaimed it with a smile. Buddy kept his nose pressed to the empty hiding place for another moment. Then he checked Sagar’s hand, in case the crust had merely been relocated.

changes.before: Buddy barked, “They’re just big dogs!” Neet corrected him: “They’re horses, you uncultured twit.”
changes.after:
Buddy barked, “They’re just big dogs!” Neet corrected him: “They’re horses, you uncultured twit.”

Buddy watched one crop a mouthful of grass. “Very big dogs.”

changes.before: Buddy rolled in the grass, delighted at every familiar smell.
changes.after: Buddy rolled in the grass, delighted at every familiar smell. At the mention of the bakery, Neet rose at once. His nostalgia had opening hours.
